body_ar: الإنسان في هذه الدنيا مأمور باستغلال حياته في طاعة الله عز وجل، ومأمور بأن لا يضيع عمره فيما لا طائل تحته، فالعمر فرصة لا تعوض، فإذا ما انقضت وذهبت ندم من لم يستغلها في طاعة الله عز وجل حين لا ينفع الندم. فاللهَ اللهَ في اغتنام الأوقات، وإعمارها بالحسنات، ومباعدة أهل الفجور والسيئات. العمر الشخصي للإنسان وكيفية استغلاله في الطاعة: الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه، ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، أما بعد: فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى جعل للإنسان حياتين: إحداهما هي هذه الدار التي هي دار عمل ولا جزاء، والأخرى هي دار الآخرة التي هي دار جزاء ولا عمل. وجعل الإنسان يبدأ بهذه الدار الدنيا التي اسمها إما أن يكون مشتقاً من الدنو لقربها، أو مشتقاً من الدناءة؛ لأنها لا تساوي عند الله جناح بعوضة..
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* A person in this world is commanded to use his life in obedience to God, mighty and majestic, and is commanded not to squander his lifetime in what has no point to it. The lifetime is an opportunity that cannot be replaced; and once it has run out and gone, whoever did not use it in obedience to God, mighty and majestic, will regret it at a time when regret is of no use. So fear God, fear God, in seizing the moments, in filling them with good deeds, and in keeping far from the people of debauchery and of evil deeds.

## The human being's personal lifetime, and how to use it in obedience

Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed:

God, glorified and exalted is He, has appointed for the human being two lives. One of them is this abode, which is an abode of work and of no recompense; the other is the abode of the hereafter, which is an abode of recompense and of no work. And He made the human being begin with this worldly abode — whose name, al-dunyā, is derived either from nearness (dunuww), because of its closeness, or from baseness (danāʾah), because it does not weigh with God as much as the wing of a gnat..

flags.context: the etymological derivation of al-dunya in the transcribed portion
options: keep the three Arabic words visible in transliteration so the derivation can be followed
render the sense only, without the Arabic
flags.note: The whole point of the sentence is that one Arabic word may come from either of two roots with opposite colourings — nearness or baseness — and it cannot be made in English without the Arabic being visible. The three words are therefore given in transliteration alongside the English senses. This is a rare case where the house rule of plain English with the term in brackets has to be extended to a word that is not a technical term, because the argument is about the word itself.

flags.context: the exhortation closing the site's synopsis
options: fear God, fear God, in seizing the moments
God, God, in seizing the moments
take heed of God in seizing the moments
flags.note: A fixed Arabic exhortation in which the divine name is doubled in the accusative, implying a suppressed verb — most naturally 'fear' or 'take heed of'. Rendered with the verb supplied, since the bare English 'God, God' would be unintelligible. The supplied verb is an expansion required by English, and is marked here as such per style guide section 1.

translator_notes: One of a run of thirteen records, IDs 688-700, all uploaded on 5 and 8-9 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/c-a-* series. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lessons were delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.
'لا تساوي عند الله جناح بعوضة' echoes a well-known prophetic report; the Sheikh does not present it as a quotation and no attribution has been added.
No ruling term appears anywhere in the record.
